title: Global smooth-section Gårding estimate for an elliptic bundle operator
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and volume form $dV$. Let $G,H\to N$ be smooth real vector bundles of the same finite rank, with smooth positive definite fibre metrics. Let $k\geq1$ be an integer and $Q:\Gamma^\infty(G)\to\Gamma^\infty(H)$ a real-linear differential operator locally of the form $Q=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}b_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$ with smooth matrix coefficients. Assume that $\sum_{|\alpha|=k}b_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha:G_x\to H_x$ is invertible whenever $0\ne\xi\in T_x^*N$. Fix a finite smooth trivializing atlas and a subordinate smooth partition of unity with compact supports in the charts. Write $\|u\|_{H^k(G)}^2$ for the sum of the Euclidean $L^2$ norms squared of all localized frame-component derivatives of $u$ through order $k$. Write $\|u\|_{L^2(G)}^2=\int_N|u|^2\,dV$ and similarly for $H$. There is a constant $C>0$, depending on these fixed data but not on $u$, such that every smooth section $u$ of $G$ satisfies $\|u\|_{H^k(G)}\leq C\bigl(\|Qu\|_{L^2(H)}+\|u\|_{L^2(G)}\bigr)$.

source.place: VI §2 Gårding inequality (2.3), Sobolev index zero, printed p.289; only its smooth-section estimate, with the two-bundle system version of VI §1; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: If $N$ is empty or the common bundle rank is zero, all sections and norms vanish and $C=1$ works. Otherwise apply [lem-sfb-differential-formal-adjoint-symbol] with $d=k$ to obtain $Q^*: \Gamma^\infty(H)\to\Gamma^\infty(G)$ of order at most $k$ and symbol $(-1)^k\sigma_k(Q)^*$. Put $B=G\oplus H$, with the orthogonal sum metric, and define $P(a,b)=(Q^*b,Qa)$. In concatenated local frames this is a real-linear differential operator on $B$ with smooth block matrix coefficients of order at most $k$.

source.place: proof (3), inherited supporting analytic branch; agent-written block-operator reduction using the existing formal-adjoint and weak-Garding nodes, not an argument stated in this blueprint file

proof.text: For $\xi\ne0$ put $A=\sigma_k(Q)(x,\xi)$ and $D=(-1)^k A^*$. Since $A:G_x\to H_x$ is invertible, $D:H_x\to G_x$ is invertible with inverse $(-1)^k(A^{-1})^*$. The degree-$k$ symbol of $P$ maps $(a,b)$ to $(Db,Aa)$; its inverse maps $(c,e)$ to $(A^{-1}e,D^{-1}c)$. Thus $P$ satisfies exactly the ellipticity hypothesis of the one-bundle weak estimate, without identifying $G$ and $H$.

proof.text: Choose a finite smooth coordinate atlas trivializing both $G$ and $H$: when the fixed atlas already trivializes $H$ take it with its cutoffs; otherwise intersect each fixed chart with trivializing opens of $H$, keep finitely many by compactness, and take a subordinate smooth partition of unity from [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition] with $S=N$, whose closed supports are compact in the charts since $N$ is compact. Write $\|\cdot\|'_{H^k}$ for the norms of the item's form built from these data, with the concatenated frames of $G,H$ for $B$. By [lem-sfb-bundle-sobolev-rellich] for the bundle $G$ and $s=k$, different atlas, frame and partition choices give equivalent norms, so there is $c\geq1$ with $\|u\|_{H^k(G)}\leq c\|u\|'_{H^k(G)}$ for all smooth $u$ ($c=1$ if the fixed data were kept). For any smooth $u$, let $w=(u,0)$. Then $Pw=(0,Qu)$ both classically and distributionally: against compactly supported smooth tests repeated integration by parts identifies distributional derivatives of smooth coefficients with their classical derivatives. Both sections are $L^2$, since they are smooth on the compact $N$. Apply [lem-sfb-weak-garding-sobolev-estimate] with bundle $B$, operator $P$, $d=k$, $s=0$, $v=w$ and the norms $\|\cdot\|'$. The base is compact, oriented and without boundary, its dimension is $m\geq1$, and $B$ has a smooth positive definite metric. The cited statement uses the integrated norm $\|\cdot\|_{L^2_g}$ of the Riemannian volume form $dV_g$ for $H^0(B)=L^2(B)$ and gives a fixed $C_0>0$ with $\|w\|'_{H^k(B)}\leq C_0(\|Pw\|_{L^2_g(B)}+\|w\|_{L^2_g(B)})$.

source.place: proof (3), inherited supporting analytic branch; agent-written block-operator reduction using the existing formal-adjoint and weak-Garding nodes, not an argument stated in this blueprint file

proof.text: For every cutoff $\chi_j$ of the chosen data and multi-index $|\alpha|\leq k$, the localized components satisfy $\partial^\alpha(\chi_j w)=(\partial^\alpha(\chi_j u),0)$. The sums of their squared Euclidean norms are identical, so $\|w\|'_{H^k(B)}=\|u\|'_{H^k(G)}$. The orthogonal sum metric gives pointwise $|w|=|u|$ and $|Pw|=|Qu|$, hence $\|w\|_{L^2_g(B)}=\|u\|_{L^2_g(G)}$ and $\|Pw\|_{L^2_g(B)}=\|Qu\|_{L^2_g(H)}$. Write $dV=\rho\,dV_g$ with $\rho$ smooth and positive ($\rho=1$ when $dV$ is the Riemannian volume form); on compact $N$ it has a minimum $\rho_->0$, so $\int|f|^2dV_g\leq\rho_-^{-1}\int|f|^2dV$ for every smooth section $f$. Combining with step 3, $\|u\|_{H^k(G)}\leq c\|u\|'_{H^k(G)}\leq cC_0\rho_-^{-1/2}(\|Qu\|_{L^2(H)}+\|u\|_{L^2(G)})$; take $C=cC_0\rho_-^{-1/2}$. All choices determining $P$, the norms and $c,\rho_-$ were fixed independently of $u$.
